  1. Description

Annotation Interface Subscribe

@Documented @Retention(CLASS) @Target(METHOD) public @interface Subscribe
Marks a method that receives events once its listener is registered: the events of the type of its parameter, and of the subtypes of that type. 
class OrderListener {
    @Subscribe
    void onPlaced(OrderPlaced event) {
        ...
    }
}

gaia-processor, on the annotation processor path, generates for each class with such methods the code that subscribes them, which calls them directly. It reports an error for a method that this code cannot call as a subscriber:

  • a private method, or one in a private nested class: the generated code is in the package of the class;
  • a static method;
  • a method of an interface;
  • a method that does not take exactly one parameter, or whose parameter is of a primitive type, an array type, a type variable or a parameterized type, or of a type that is not accessible from the package of the class;
  • a method that does not return void;
  • a method that declares checked exceptions;
  • a method that overrides a @Subscribe method, or one with a subscribing annotation: registering the listener subscribes the overridden method, which calls the overriding one, so annotating both would deliver each event twice. Overriding such a method without the annotation is enough;
  • a method that also has a subscribing annotation.

javac hands annotation processors no method of a local or anonymous class, so the processor cannot report the annotation there, and generates nothing for it: registering an instance of such a class subscribes only the methods of the classes it extends.

The annotation is retained in class files, so that the processor sees it on the methods of classes compiled before, but not at run time: nothing reads it by reflection.
